आरिष्टनेमि: Āriṣṭanemi (VI) — a son of Citraka; daughter Sumati, wife of Sagara. Br. III. 71. 115; Vā. 88. 156, 159; 96. 114.
आकर्णनी: Ākarṇanī — the goddess following Revatī. M. 179. 72.
आकर्षिणी: Ākarṣiṇī — a mudrā Devī. Br. IV. 42. 6.
आकार: Ākāra — the second face of the fourteen faced Deva, Manu Svārociṣa born in white colour. Vā. 26. 33.
आकाश: Ākāśa (I) — a god to be worshipped in housebuilding. M. 253. 24; 265. 39.
Ākāśa (II) — with Dik; a sthāna of Rudra; son, Sarga. Vi. I. 8. 7-11.
आकाशम्: Ākāśam — the ether, stands uncovered, formless, devoid of rasa, sparśa and gandha; its characteristic is śabda. Vā. 102. 15, 17; M. 3. 23.
आकाशगङ्गा: Ākāśagaṅgā — R. that encircles Amarāvatī;1 that water which comes down without the cloud; bath in this is called celestial ablution.2 1) Bhā. VIII. 15. 14. 2) Vi. II. 9. 12 and 17.
आकूति: Ākūti (I) — A daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu (Vai-rāja-Vā. P.) and Śatarūpā. Wife of Ruci. From her Hari manifested himself for imparting dharma and jñāna. Gave birth to twins — a son and a daughter by putrikādharma. These were Yajña and Dakṣiṇā. Bhā. I. 3. 12; III. 12. 55-56; IV. 1. 1-4; VIII. 1. 5; II. 7. 2; Br. III. 3. 113; Vā. 10. 17-9; Br. I. 1. 58; II. 9. 42-43; Vi. I. 7. 18-19.
Ākūti (II) — the queen of Sarvatejas and mother of Manu Cākṣuṣa. Bhā. IV. 13. 15.
Ākūti (IV) — a Jayādeva. Br. III. 3. 6; 4. 2; Vā. 66. 6.
Ākūti (VI) — became twins in the Ākūti kalpa. Vā. 21. 55-56.
Ākūti (VII) — a son of Brahman with a mantraśarīra Vā. 67. 4-5.
Ākūti (VIII) — the mother of Yajña, the mindborn son in the first epoch of Manu. Vi. III. 1. 36.
आकृति: Ākṛti (I) — a progenitor, responsible for form and shape. Br. II. 9. 1 and 7.
Ākṛti (II) — a son of Babhru. Br. III. 70. 38.
आखण्डल: Ākhaṇḍala — name of Indra. Bhā. III. 33. 20.
आख्यानम्: Ākhyānam — a feature of the Purāṇa the fifth Veda;1 Purāṇic stories.2 1) Br. II. 34. 21; III. 1. 6; 5. 8 and 11; 13. 54; 59. 4; Vā. 54. 1; 60. 21; 67. 54, 58. 2) M. 53. 65; 214. 23; Vi. I. 22. 84; III. 6. 15.
आगम: Āgama1 — the rules of;2 for digging wells, constructing tanks and gardens;3 cited for yajñas where paśu was not involved and where bīja (seeds) served the purpose of the animal.4 1) Vi. I. 17. 58. 2) Br. II. 30. 19 and 27; III. 21. 46. 3) M. 58. 55; 143. 13. 4) Vā. 53. 122; 57. 100.
आगस्त्य: Āgastyas — the Brahmarākṣasas — a clan moving about in the night;1 of Surabhi forest;2 summoned Kauberaka to live at Hariśṛṅga.3 1) Br. III. 8. 59 and 62; Vā. 69. 195-6. 2) M. 121. 62. 3) Vā. 47. 60-1.
आगावह: Āgāvaha — a son of Vasudeva and Vṛkadevī a mahātmā. Br. III. 71. 180.
आगाही: Āgāhī — a daughter of Vṛkadevī. Vā. 96. 180.
आग्नायि: Āgnāyi — a goddess, wife of Dikpāla Agni. M. 286. 7.
आग्नीध्र: Āgnīdhra (I) — a son of Priyavrata and Barhiṣmatī. Father of Nābhi. Appointed lord of Jambūdvīpa.1 Pro-tected the people like his children. Issueless, he performed tapas when Brahmā sent the divine damsel Pūrvacitti with whom Āgnīdhra enjoyed life for 100,000 years. After giv-ing birth to nine sons, she went back to the court of Brahmā. He divided his kingdom among his sons, and rejoined his wife in another world. On his death, his nine sons married the nine daughters of Meru.2 1) Bhā. XI. 2. 15; V. 1. 25 and 33. 2) Ib. V. 2. 1-23; Br. II. 14. 44-53; Vi. II. 1. 7, 12, 16-24.
Ā(A)gnīdhra (II) — one of the ten sons of Svāyam-bhuva Manu;1 milked the Cow-Earth with Svāyambhuva as calf.2 1) Br. II. 13. 104; M. 9. 4. 2) Vā. 63. 13.
Āgnīdhra (III) — one of the ten sons of the daughter of Kardama, and Priyavrata. Br. II. 14. 9.
आग्निध्र: Āgnidhra (IV) — one of the 16 Ṛtviks for an Yajña; created from the hands of Nārāyaṇa. M. 167. 10.
आग्नीध्रक: Āgnīdhraka — a sage of the epoch of the XIIth Manu. Bhā. VIII. 13. 28.
आग्निवेश्यायन: Āgniveśyāyanas — a Brahma-kula originating from Jātūkarṇa. Bhā. IX. 2. 22.
आग्नेय: Āgneya (II) — a division of the night. Vā. 66. 43.
Āgneyas (I) — the Gandharva followers of Kubera;1 their residences on the southern peaks of Maryādā Parvata.2 1) Vā. 40. 8. 2) Vā. 40. 5.
Āgneyas (II) — the Aṅgiras adopted by Agni when they sprung out of the sacrificial fire of Vāruṇī-yajña. Vā. 65. 42.
आग्नेयपुराण: Āgneya-Purāṇa — one among the eighteen Purāṇas;1 deals with Īśāna Kalpa; narrated by Agni to Vasiṣṭha: of 16,000 verses; its gift and fruits thereof.2 1) Bhā. XII. 7. 23. 2) M. 53. 28-30.
आग्नेयव्रतम्: Āgneya-vratam — of kings; ruin rebellious sāmantas by his valour. M. 226. 7.
आग्नेयास्त्रम्: Āgneyāstram — given to Sagara by Bhārgava (Aurva). Vā. 88. 124 and 135; Vi. IV. 3. 37.
आग्नेयि: Āgneyi (I) — the city of Agni. Bhā. X. 89. 44.
आग्नेयी: Āgneyī (II) — the wife of Havirdhāna, and mother of six children: also known as Dhiṣaṇā. Br. II. 37. 23; Vā. 63. 23; Vi. I. 14. 2; M. 4. 45.
Āgneyī (III) — the wife of Ūru. M. 4. 43.
Āgneyī (IV) — the wife of Kuru and mother of six sons. Vi. I. 13. 6.
आग्रयणम्: Āgrayaṇam — a Pitṛ ritual; offering of śyāmāka and sugar;1 the first Soma libation at the Agniṣṭoma sacrifice.2 1) Br. III. 14. 9; Vā. 78. 8. 2) Vā. 75. 6.
आङ्गिरस: Āṅgirasa — a teacher of Atharva Veda. (Āṅgirasa kalpa Burnouf). Bhā. XII. 7. 4.
आङ्गिरसम्: Āṅgirasam — a sacrifice performed by Brāhmaṇas near Brindāvana. Bhā. X. 23. 3.
आङ्गिरसी: Āṅgirasī — the wife of Vasu and mother of Viśva-karman. Bhā. VI. 6. 15.
आचमनम्: Ācamanam — the mode and significance of;1 occasions for performing Ācamanam.2 1) Vā. 79. 42-47. 2) Ib. 79. 37-42.
आचार्य: Ācāryas — qualifications of; old, selfless, highly learned, humble, well disciplined, truthful, etc.; he who by himself follows the rules of good conduct and thus establishes the ācāra and thinks of the truth of the Śāstra by yamas and niyamas. Br. II. 32. 30-32; IV. 8. 5; M. 145. 28-29; Vā. 59. 28-30.
आजगर: Ājagara — a vrata followed by Ṛṣabha when he became a mendicant. Bhā. V. 5. 32.

Ājagara — a sage. Praḥlāda saw him one day lying on the bare ground on a cliff of the Sahya hills, and bowed to him. Praḥlāda asked the sage how he who had no com-forts was able to maintain a sound body. The sage replied that he had renounced all desires, learning renunciation from the bee and contentment from the serpent, while his mind was ever absorbed in Hari. Bhā. VII. 13. 11-18, 20-45.
आजगव: Ājagava — the bow of Pṛthu;1 of Śiva.2 1) Br. II. 36. 148; Vā. 62. 127; Vi. I. 13. 40 and 69. 2) Br. III. 65. 32.
आजन: Ājana — a nephew of Hiraṇyakaśipu. M. 6. 27.
आजपाल: Ājapāla — a son of Aja and father of Daśaratha. M. 12. 49.
आजानेय: Ājāneya — the country noted for horses. Br. IV. 16. 17.
आजिगर्त: Ājigarta — Śunaḥśepa, the son of Ajigarta — (see Aji-garta, s.v.). Bhā. IX. 16. 30; IX. 7. 20-21.
आजीवक: Ājīvaka — a heretic sect. Br. III. 14. 39.
आज्ञा: Ājñā — a name of Lalitā. Br. IV. 17. 19.
आज्य: Ājya (I) — good to be seen first after rising from one's bed;1 as a sacrificial offering.2 1) Bhā. X. 70. 12; Vā. 29. 30. 2) Br. IV. 1. 98; Vā. 100. 103.
Ājya (II) — one of the nine sons of Sāvarṇi. Vā. 100. 22.
Ājyas — four kinds of. Br. IV. 1. 98-100.
आज्यप: Ājyapas — a class of Manes who reside in regions belong-ing to Kardama Prajāpati, descendants of Pulaha; Virajā, wife of Nahuṣa was their mindborn daughter; largely wor-shipped by Vaiśyas. Br. II. 28. 19; III. 10. 93-5; Bhā. IV. 1. 63; M. 102. 21; Vā. 30. 100; 56. 17; 73. 43; 101. 43.
आटव्य: Āṭavyas — the people of a southern country. Br. II. 16. 57; M. 114. 48; Vā. 45. 126.
आडम्बर: Āḍambara — Instrument of war music. M. 137. 29; 138. 3.
आडि: Āḍi — a son of Asura Andhaka; to wreak vengeance on Śiva for having slain his father, he entered the harem of Śiva in the guise of a snake, and assumed the guise of Umā before him. He could change his form twice as he liked owing to a boon from Brahmā; but the second change would be followed by death. On close examination, Śiva dis-covered the figure to be the Asura in disguise, threw the Vajra and slew him. M. 156. 12-37.
आडिबक: Āḍib(v)aka — the sixth war of gods and Asuras.1 In this Kakustha helped Indra;2 the sixth of the twelve incar-nations of Hari.3 1) Br. III. 72. 74. 2) Vā. 88. 25. 3) M. 47. 34-35 and 44; Vā. 97. 81.
आण्डकोश: Āṇḍakośa — comprised of sixteen vikāras and eight prakṛtis. 50 crores of yojanas in breadth in the interior. Outside encircled by seven sheaths of the earth and other elements. Bhā. III. 11. 39-41; 20. 15; II. 1. 25.
आण्डीर: Āṇḍīra (I) — the son of Sarūpya. Father of Pāṇḍya, Kerala, Chola and Kulya. Br. III. 74. 5-6.
Āṇḍīra (II) — the son of Varūtha. M. 48. 4.
आततायिन्: Ātatāyins — Those who set fire to buildings, administer poison, lift their weapons to strike, or practise ābhicāra or become talebearers or seditionists. M. 227. 116-9.
आतप: Ātapa — a son of Uṣā and Vibhāvasu. A Vasu. Father of Pañcayāma. Bhā. VI. 6. 16.
आत्म: Ātma — has no guṇas. Twelve characteristics of. Bhā. I. 18. 50; VII. 1. 7-9; 7. 19-20.
आत्मज: Ātmaja — a son of Svarbhānu and Prabhā. Vā. 92. 2.
आत्मभू: Ātmabhū — name of Brahmā. Bhā. III. 12. 20.
आत्मवत्: Ātmavat — a mantrakṛt;1 the son of Cyavana Bhārgava; married Ruci; Father of Nahuṣa.2 1) Br. II. 32. 104; M. 145. 98; Vā. 59. 96. 2) Vā. 65. 90-91.
आत्मविद्या: Ātmavidyā — the Vedānta;1 symbolical of Devī.2 1) M. 215. 54. 2) Vi. I. 9. 120.
आत्मा: Ātmā — that which is attained, which is taken away and that which is, and hence the ever present bhāva. Vā. 5. 34-5.
आत्माकर्षणिका: Ātmākarṣaṇikā — a Gupta Śakti. Br. IV. 19. 20.
आत्मायु: Ātmāyu — a son of Aṅgirasa. M. 196. 2.
आत्यन्तिक: Ātyantika — one of the three movements of creatures. Vā. 1. 161; 100. 132.
Ātyantika kalpa — one division of Brahma kalpa. Vā. 100. 134.
आत्रेय: Ātreya — a pupil of Sūta;1 the last reference is to the sage in the Raivatamanvantara.2 Sage of the Tāmasa man-vantara.3 Ātreya Śaradvata one of the seven sages;4 Ātre-yavāruni,5 Niṣprakampa,6 Sūtapūḥ.7 1) Va. 61. 56. 2) Vā. 62. 17, 54. 3) Vā. 62. 41. 4) Vā. 100. 11. 5) Vā. 100. 82. 6) Vā. 100. 107. 7) Vā. 100. 96; 106. 39.
Ātreyas (I) — a deva gaṇa of the Pitṛs, like Svastyātreya, Br. III. 1. 51; 8. 81.
Ātreyas (II) — the five sons of Atri and Anasūyā; Saty-netra, Havya, Āpomūrṭi, Śanīśvara and Soma. Vā. 28. 18-20; Br. II. 11. 23-24.
आथर्वणीश्रुति: Ātharvaṇī(a)śruti — is Atharva Veda. Vi. VI. 5. 65; Vā. 76. 1.
आदर्श: Ādarśa (I) — its use for dressing. Devahūtī used it to dress herself;1 auspicious to look at in the morning.2 1) Bhā. III. 23. 30. 2) Br. III. 28. 10; Vi. III. 11. 22; Bhā. X. 70. 11.
Ādarśa (II) — a son of the Third Sāvarṇa Manu. Br. IV. 1. 81; Vā. 100. 84.
आदिगदाधर: Ādigadādhara — Viṣṇu; bore for the first time the gadā out of the bone of Gadā-asura. He is Vyakta, the whole universe appearing in him in the gayā śilā; in praise of, by Brahmā and Śiva. Vā. 109. 13-17, 25, 27-31, 41-42 and 43-50; 111. 16.
आदिकूर्म: Ādikūrma — created by Lalitā to consume waters due to Bhaṇḍa's arṇavāstram. Br. IV. 29. 92.
आदिकेशव: Ādikeśava — a name of Viṣṇu. Br. IV. 15. 18.
आदित्य: Āditya (I) — patronymic of Vidhātṛ. Bhā. VI. 18. 3.
Āditya (II) — a name of Sūrya (s.v.);1 presented the jewel Syamantaka to Satrājit.2 1) Br. II. 21. 3; M. 2. 31-4. 2) Vi. IV. 13. 11.
Āditya (III) — from ādāna receiving waters and letting them off; kālāgni, pitāmaha and soma, all prapitāmahas;1 same as Rudra; see Rudra.2 1) Vā. 12. 37; 31. 29-35. 2) Br. II. 10. 22.
Āditya (IV) — a division of the night. Vā. 66. 44.

Ādityas — sons of Aditi and Kaśyapa, originally Vai-kuṇṭhas and Sādhyas;1 Gods of the Vaivasvata epoch at the commencement of the first Tretāyuga, known as Jayadevas;2 twelve in number; were known as Tuṣitas in the Cākṣuṣa epoch.3 Names were Indra, Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, Yama, Vivasvat, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Amśumat, and Viṣṇu.4 Born of Viṣṇu as their overlord.5 Escorted Indra; vanquished Diti's sons, and vanquished by Rāvaṇa;6 came with gods to Dvārakā to request Kṛṣṇa to leave for Vai-kuṇṭha.7 One of the names of the first Marut Gaṇa.8 Born with Rudras.9 Residents of Bhuvarloka.10 Offered pre-sents (upāyana) at the time of the marriage of Kāmeśvara with Lalitā.11 Praised Lalitā when Bhaṇḍa was killed.12 1) Br. II. 38. 3; III. 1. 61; 3. 57-61, 67-8; 4. 34; M. 171. 55; Vā. 30. 83, 99, 163; 39. 49; 64. 2; 66. 60, 66-7; Vi. I. 15. 129. 2) Bhā. VIII. 13. 4; VI. 7. 2; 10. 17; M. 9. 29. 3) Vā. 67. 44; M. 6. 3; Vi. I. 15. 132. 4) Bhā. XII. 11. 30-45; Br. II. 24. 33-4, 75; 26-42; M. 132. 3; 247. 10; Vi. I. 15. 130-1. 5) Vi. V. 1. 17-8; 4. 5; Bhā. XII. 11. 30f; XI. 16. 13. Br. III. 8. 5. 6) Br. III. 5. 48; 7. 254. 7) Bhā. XI. 6. 2. 8) Vā. 67. 123. 9) Ib. 65. 61. 10) Ib. 101. 30; Br. IV. 2. 28-9. 11) Br. IV. 15. 24. 12) Ib. IV. 30. 8.
Āditya Vamśa — the solar race. M. 11. 1.
आदित्यत्वम्: Ādityatvam — the right of being born as sons of Aditi. Vā. 66. 59.
आदित्यमण्डल: Ādityamaṇḍala — the Yajus returned to possession of Sūrya when Yājñavalkya surrounded them. Vā. 61. 21.
आदित्यवर्त्मा: Ādityavartmā — by this the divine weapons of Kṛṣṇa went to heaven. Vi. V. 37. 52.
आदित्यवारम्: Ādityavāram — Sunday, fit for Anaṅgadeva vratam; in-auspicious for housebuilding;1 devoted to worship of Sūrya, Candra and Agni.2 1) M. 70. 46; 253. 7. 2) M. 97. 3-20.
आदित्यशयनम्: Ādityaśayanam — a vow in honour of Śaṅkara in the name of Sūrya; auspicious day is Sunday preferably with constellation Hasta; accompanied by gifts to Brāhmaṇas: Relieves one from bondage of birth; practised by Vasiṣṭha, Arjuna, Kubera, Indra in olden days. M. 55. 3-33.
आदित्येशम्: Ādityeśam — a tīrtha on the Narmadā. M. 191. 5.
आदिदेव: Ādidevas — seven gaṇas of which three are without form and four are with form; above them are three Bhāvamūrtis and below them four sūkṣmamūrtis. Vā. 71. 54-6.
आदिपाल: Ādipāla — a name of Viṣṇu. Vā. 109. 15.
आदिपुराणम्: Ādipurāṇam — Ten thousand and six hundred ślokas. Vā. 104. 7.
आदिसर्ग: Ādisarga — origin of,1 described;2 the primary creation.3 1) Br. II. 10. 2. 2) Ib. II. Ch. 9. 3) M. 8. 1; 52. 2.
आद्य: Ādyas — a group of gods of Cākṣuṣa epoch, eight in number. Br. II. 36. 66 and 69.
Ādya Pratīhāri — the first servant maid of Śiva with four arms and six white clothes; behind are other ladies to honour Śaṅkara. Vā. 101. 274-7.
आधन: Ādhana — one of the seven sons of Vasiṣṭha. Vā. 28. 36.
आधार: Ādhāra cakra — Into this Hari enters. Bhā. XI. 12. 17.
आधाराधेयभाव: Ādhārādheyabhāva — By this avikāras became vikāras. Earth, etc., are vikāras. Br. II. 19. 181-2.
आद्ध: Āddha — a pupil of Yājñavalkya. Br. II. 35. 28.
आध्यात्मकी: Ādhyātmakī Vidyā — the knowledge of Ātman taught by Kapila to his mother Devahūti; also Ānvīkṣikī. Bhā. III. 24. 40; 25. 4, 13-15.
आध्वर्यवम्: Ādhvaryavam — 12000 chandas; from Yajus; uttered by the Adhvaryu in an yajña. Vā. 58. 15; 60. 15-16; 61. 64; Vi. III. 4. 12.
आनक: Ānaka (I) — a son of Śūra and Māriṣā. Married Kankā and had two sons — Satyajit and Purujit. Bhā. IX. 24. 28 and 41.
Ānaka (II) — a kind of divine musical instrument. Bhā. X. 83. 30; M. 135. 83. 140-43; Vā. 96. 145; Br. III. 71. 147.
आनकदुन्दुभी: Ānakadundubhī — a previous name of Vasudeva. (s.v.)1 When he was born Dundubhi and the Ānakas were sounded as in a festival in the house of Śūra by the gods;2 at Nandagopagṛha.3 Son of Anu.4 Entered fire after the departure of Rāma and Kṛṣṇa to Heaven.5 1) Br. III. 71. 146, 164. 217; M. 46. 2 and 11; Vi. V. 2. 8 and 16. 2) Vā. 96. 144-5; Vi. IV. 14. 29. 3) Vā. 96. 211. 4) Vi. IV. 14. 14. 5) Vi. V. 38. 4.
आनकदुन्दुभि: Ānakadundubhis — divine musicians, played at the birth of Vesudeva. Vi. IV. 14. 28.
आनका: Ānakā — a son of Ugrasena. Vi. IV. 14. 20.
आनन्द: Ānanda (I) (c) — a kingdom adjoining the Dundubhi hill in Plakṣadvīpa. Br. II. 14. 39; 17. 16.
Ānanda (II) — a Satya god. Br. II. 36. 35.
Ānanda (III) — The Lord of first kalpa consisting 100 lakhs of years by name Bhāva; this is the place of Brahmā. Vā. 21. 28.
Ānanda (IV) — a son of Medhātithi; a varṣa after his name, in Plakṣadvīpa. Vā. 33. 32; Vi. II. 4. 4 and 5.
आनन्दम्: Ānandam — a varṣa centering round the Dundubhi hill of Plakṣa. Vā. 49. 14.
आनन्दकम्: Ānandakam — same as Anicakam varṣam. M. 122. 23.
आनन्दजलम्: Ānandajalam — a lake in the Jātudha hill of pure and crystal waters; here lives Caṇḍa, the lord of the Nāgas. Vā. 41. 68-73.
आनन्दव्रतम्: Ānandavratam — in honour of Brahmā. M. 101. 32.
आनर्त: Ānarta (I) (c) — a western country; that of Kṛṣṇa;1 on the way from Dvāraka to Indraprastha.2 Its king went to Syamantapañcaka for solar eclipse.3 Destroyed by Dvivida;4 named after Śaryāti; its capital Kuśasthalī.5 1) Bhā. I. 11. 1. 2) Ib. X. 71. 21. 3) Ib. X. 82. 13; Br. II. 16. 62; M. 12. 22. 4) Ib. X. 67. 4. 5) Vā. 86. 24; Vi. IV. 1. 64.

Ānarta (II) — a son of Śaryāti and father of Reva(ta).1 Rocamāna was his son; ruled over the kingdom of Ānarta from Kuśasthalī.2 1) Bhā. IX. 3. 27; Br. III. 61. 18; Vā. 86. 23-24; Vi. IV. 1. 63-4. 2) M. 12. 21-2.
Ānarta (III) — a son of Vītihotra. M. 43. 49.

Ānartas — people of Ānarta over whom Revata ruled.1 Heard of Kṛṣṇa going to Mithilā and met him on the way with presents;2 of the south.3 1) Bhā. I. 10, 35; 14. 25; IX. 3. 28; X. 52. 15; M. 114. 51. 2) Bhā. X. 86. 20. 3) Vā. 45. 131.
आनर्तपुरी: Ānartapurī — the capital of Ānarta — Dvāraka; from here Kṛṣṇa went to Vidarbha in one night. Bhā. I. 14. 25; X. 53. 6.
आन्त्यायन: Āntyāyana — a son of Bhṛgu, and a deva. Br. III. 1. 89.
आन्दोलिकनियुद्धम्: Āndolika-niyuddham — swinging on the hands of friends and boxing; by Kṛṣṇa and Rāma. Vi. V. 9. 8.
आन्धक: Āndhaka — a son of Vipracitti and Simhikā. Vi. I. 21. 12.
आन्धकार: Āndhakāra (c) — a kingdom after the name of Andha-kāra,1 near Pīvara hill.2 1) Br. II. 14. 25. 2) Ib. II. 19. 72.
आन्ध्र: Āndhras (I) — the kings of Andhra dynasty, thirty in number, ruled the earth for 456 years. Seven of them were contemporaries of seven Kauśalas, chiefs of Vidūra and Niṣa-dhas;1 According to Matsya Purāṇa, 19 members of the dynasty ruled for 460 years. Kingdoms of Ārya and Mleccha existed side by side — Ābhīras, Gardabhilas, Śakas, Yavanas, Tuṣāras, Guruṇḍas, and Hūṇas.2 1) Bhā. XII. 1. 22-28 and 35. 2) M. 272. 37; 273. 16-19, 25.

Āndhras (II) — a tribe purified by the worship of Hari.1 Enlisted by Jarāsandha against the Yadus;2 a southern country unfit for performing Śrāddha.3 1) Bhā. II. 4. 18. 2) Bhā. X. [50 (V) 3]. 3) Br. II. 16. 59; III. 14. 80; IV. 29. 131.
आन्ध्रभृत्य: Āndhrabhṛtyas — seven in number. Vi. IV. 24. 51.
आनृहवान्: Ānṛhavān — a rājaṛṣi becoming a Brāhmaṇa. Vā. 91. 116.
आन्वीक्षिकि: Ānvīkṣiki (Adhyātmakī vidyā, s.v.) — Taught by Dat-tātreya to Alarka and others.1 Produced by Brahmā.2 Helps concentration on the Absolute.3 Learnt by Rāma and Kṛṣṇa.4 Symbolical of Devī.5 1) Bhā. I. 3. 11; M. 215. 54; Vi. V. 10. 27. 2) Bhā. III. 12. 44; 25. 4. 3) Ib. XI. 20. 24. 4) Ib. X. 45. 34. 5) Vi. I. 9. 121.
आह्निकक्रम: Āhnikakrama — the daily routine of duties. Vā. 53. 39; Vi. V. 18. 34.
आप: Āpa (I) — a vyāpaka. ety. of; came out of Agni, when the latter was lost in the earth. Br. I. 5. 131-5; II. 6. 56-7; 20. 1 and 5; Vā. 6. 1.
Āpa (II) — a Rākṣasa with the Śarat sun. Br. II. 23. 15; Vā. 52. 15.
Āpa (III) — a son of Vasiṣṭha, and a Prajāpati of the Svārociṣa epoch. M. 9. 9.

Āpa (IV) — is Bhava; hence do not commit nuisance in waters; nor bathe naked, nor have sexual intercourse in water; forsake colourless, tasteless and small waters; their source is the ocean and hence they must not be stopped in their progress to it. Vā. 27. 21-7.
आपक: Āpakas — certain grahas which cause fear to children. Vā. 69. 191.
आपन: Āpana (c) — a kingdom to which Puramjana went by the entrance Mukhyā; allegorically Vyavahāra. Bhā. IV. 25. 49; 29. 12.
आपनाप: Āpanāpa — a pupil of Bāṣkali. Br. II. 35. 6.
आपव: Āpava (Vasiṣṭha) (I) — a sage of the time of second Sāvarṇa Manu.1 Finding his hermit destroyed by Kārta-vīrya's fire, cursed that he would be slain by Paraśurāma.2 Resident of Hematālavanam.3 1) Br. IV. 1. 70. 2) Ib. III. 69. 44-5; M. 44. 1. 12-14. 3) M. 43. 41.

Āpava (II) — the son of Varuṇa; cursed Kārtavīryārjuna who allowed his tapovana to be consumed by Citrabhānu; for ages past he was performing penance at the place, living on water. Vā. 94. 43; 95. 11-13.
आपवत्स: Āpavatsa — to be worshipped in housebuildings. M. 253. 31; 268. 20.
आपस्तम्ब: Āpastamba — acted as priest in the Putreṣṭi of Diti. M. 7. 33-4; 192. 60.
आपस्तम्बि: Āpastambi — a Bhārgava, of Āṅgirasapravara. M. 195. 33; 196. 18.
आपादबद्ध: Āpādabaddha — the son of Śātakarṇi, ruled for 30 years. Vā. 99. 351.
आपानगोष्ठि: Āpānagoṣṭhi — Revelry and mirth in the assembly of Kṛṣṇa with 16000 ladies; of Apsaras with Gandharvas. M. 70. 4; 120. 31.
आपीतक: Āpītaka — son of Lambodara Āndhra, ruled for 12 years. M. 273. 5.
आपूरण: Āpūraṇa (I) — the Yakṣa who resides in the sun's chariot during the month of Bhādrapada. Vi. II. 10. 10.
Āpūraṇa (II) — a Nāga (Dhṛtarāṣṭra). Vā. 69. 72; Vi. IV. 8. 45.
आपोमयदेव: Āpomayadeva — worshipped in Krauñcadvīpa. Bhā. V. 20. 22-3.
आपोमूर्ति: Āpomūrti — an Ātreya; a sage of the epoch of the second Sāvarṇa Manu. Br. II. 11. 23; IV. 1. 70; Vā. 28. 20.
आपोलव: Āpolava — the son of Śāntakarṇi; ruled for 12 years. Br. III. 74. 163.
आप्तोर्याम: Āptoryāma — a sacrifice1 created from the west face of Brahmā.2 (north face-Vi. P.). 1) Bhā. III. 12. 40. 2) Vi. I. 5. 56.
आप्नुवान: Āpnuvāna — a son of Bhṛgu and a gotrakara; a pravara of Bhārgava gotra; Father of Aurva. M. 195. 15 and 29.
आप्य: Āpya (II) — a particular period of the day. Vā. 66. 40.
Āpyas — one of the gaṇas of the eight gods of the Cāk-ṣuṣa epoch. Bhā. VIII. 5. 8; Vi. III. 1. 27.
आप्यायन: Āpyāyana — a territorial division of Śālmalidvīpa. Bhā. V. 20. 9.
आप्यायनम्: Āpyāyanam — a particular offering to Agni, Soma and Yama in the Śrāddha ritual. First to Pitṛs and then to Devas, as Pitṛs are Pūrvadevatas. M. 15. 32-41; 16. 33; 17. 58.
आप्रवान: Āpravāna — a son of Cyavana; married Ṛci, daughter of Nahuṣa: Father of Aurva, born from her thigh. Br. III. 1. 93-5.
आबाधविस्तर: Ābādhavistara — of the earth; one crore in every direc-tion from Meru as centre; also calculated in another way. Vā. 50. 69-70.
आब्रह्मस्तम्बपर्यन्तम्: Ābrahmastambaparyantam — from Brahmā to grass. Vā. 110. 21, 64.
आभिचार: Ābhicāra — Incantations done by Purohita and ministers for defeating the enemy — according to Bhaṇḍa;1 Brhaspati did this on behalf of Indra to vanquish Rāji's sons.2 1) Br. IV. 21. 97. 2) Vi. IV. 9. 19.
आभिल: Ābhila — a mahāratha, and a commander of Bhaṇḍa's army. His riding vehicle was Simha. Br. IV. 29. 21-2.
आभीर: Ābhīra — country of Ābhīras.1 Dvijas of, became vrātyas after Puramjaya's days.2 Purified of sin by devotion to Hari.3 Seven of this tribe ruled from Avabhṛti.4 The Braḥmāṇḍa and Vāyu say ten of them ruled after the Āndhras;5 for 67 years. 1) Bhā. I. 10. 35; Br. II. 16. 46 and 57; 18. 48. 2) Bhā. XII 1. 38. 3) Ib. II. 4. 18. 4) Bhā. XII. 1. 29; Vā. 99. 359; Vi. IV. 24. 51, 68. 5) Br. III. 74. 174; M. 50. 76; 114. 40; 163. 72; 273. 18.

Ābhīras — a tribe of Dakṣiṇāpatha saw Arjuna singly carrying much wealth and women and attacked him; he took up his Gāṇḍiva and found he had lost its secret and power;1 freebooters and shepherds of the Pañcanada country who lived in villages; mlecchas; chief weapons of, staves and cudgels.2 1) Vā. 45. 115, 126; 47. 46; 99. 269; Vi. II. 3. 16. 2) Vi. V. 38. 14-28, 50-52.
आभीरकन्या: Ābhīrakanyā — observed the Kalyāṇinī vratam and became Urvaśī of the Heaven. M. 69. 59.
आभूतरजस: Ābhūtarajasa — gods of the Raivata epoch. M. 9. 20.
आभ्रहमु: Ābhrahamu — a son of Bhadra. Vā. 69. 213.
आम: Āma (I) — a son of Ghṛtapṛṣṭha. Bhā. V. 20. 21.
Āma (II) — a son of Kṛṣṇa and (Satyā) daughter of Nagnacit. Bhā. X. 61. 13.
आमगर्भ: Āmagarbhas — Pitṛs dead as small children. Vā. 110. 53.
आमपात्रम्: Āmapātram — the milking vessel of the Yakṣas. Br. II. 36. 215; Vā. 62. 182.
आमान्नम्: Āmānnam — gift of uncooked food in a śrāddha, gene-rally by Śūdras; also Āmaśrāddham; forbidden for yatis. M. 17. 70; Vā. 18. 20.
आमोद: Āmoda — a vighna nāyaka. Br. IV. 27. 81; 44. 68.
आम्नायनाथा: Āmnāyanāthā — a name of Lalitā. Br. IV. 18. 17.
आम्ब: Āmba — a son of Kṛṣṇa. Bhā. I. 10. 29.
आम्बिकेय: Āmbikeya (I) — a place where Hiraṇyākṣa was slain by Vārāha Hari. M. 122. 16.
Āmbikeya (II) — a hill of the Śākadvīpam. Vā. 49. 84; Vi. II. 4. 62.
आम्र: Āmra — the mango tree in Brahmasaras, in the shape of Brahmā; he who waters the tree will lead the Pitṛs to salvation. Vā. 43. 6; 111. 35-36.
आम्रवनम्: Āmravanam — between Viśākha and Pataṅga hills. Vā. 38. 18-22.
आम्रातकेश्वरम्: Āmrātakeśvaram — a tīrtham on the Narmadā sacred to Pitṛs, and to Śiva. M. 22. 51; 181. 28; 190. 5.
आय: Āya — a Tuṣita god. Br. II. 36. 11.
आयतनम्: Āyatanam of Deva — called divyam by the Veda, at the end of Nirāloka and of ākāśa or ether: Inaccessible to gods.1 Temples as places for śrāddha; construction of: description shows the Vaiṣṇava and Śaiva shrines in the same com-pound.2 Shrines where Purāṇas were read.3 1) Br. II. 19. 168-9; III. 11. 34. 2) M. 17. 11; 58. 2; 83. 3; 105. 15; 268. 35; 270. 34. 3) Vā. 4. 7; 30. 150; 38. 31, 48, 58; 54. 3; 77. 63; 92. 52.
आयति: Āyati (I) — a daughter of Meru and Dharaṇi, wife of Dhātṛ (Vidhātṛ-Vā. P.) and mother of Mṛkaṇḍa;1 mother of Prāṇa also.2 1) Bhā. IV. 1. 43-44; Vā. 28. 4; 30. 34; Vi. I. 10. 3. 2) Br. II. 11. 5-6; 13. 37.
Āyati (II) — a son of Nahuṣa. Bhā. IX. 18. 1; Br. III. 68. 12; Vā. 93. 13; Vi. IV. 10. 1.
आयसम्पात्रम्: Āyasampātram — the iron vessel sacred to Asuras. Br. II. 36. 210; M. 10. 20.
आयाप्य: Āyāpya — a mantrakṛt and of Aṅgirasa branch. Vā. 59. 101.
आयु: Āyu (I) — a son of Prāṇa and Ūrjasvatī: a Vasu;1 Father of Vaitaṇḍya and others.2 1) Bhā. VI. 6. 12. 2) Br. III. 3. 21, 24.
Āyu (II) — the son of Puruhotra, and father of Sātvata. Bhā. IX. 24. 6.

Āyu (III) — one of the six sons of Purūravas and Urvaśī; wife Prabhā, Rāhu's daughter; father of five sons, Nahuṣa, Vṛddhaśarman, Rāju, Dambha, and Vipāpman, all of them expert warriors. Bhā. IX. 15. 1; 17. 1; Br. III. 66. 22, 90; 67. 1; M. 24. 33-5; Vā. 91. 51; Vi. IV. 6. 73; 7. 1; 8. 1-3.
Āyu (IV) — a son of Kṛṣṇa and Bhadrā. Bhā. X. 61. 17.
Āyu (V) — The sage presiding over the month of Puṣya. Bhā. XII. 11. 42.
Āyu (VI) — (Śuci Agni). Father of Mahiṣa. Br. II. 12. 38-40.
Āyu (VIII) — the Agni that lives in Paśu. Vā. 29. 37.
Āyu (IX) — a son of Aṅgirasa; father of Amāvasu. Vā. 65. 105; 73. 5.
आयुतायु: Āyutāyu — the son of Sindhudvīpa. M. 12. 46; Vā. 88. 173.
आयुध: Āyudhas — weapons of war, enumerated and described. Br. IV. 22. 10-14; M. 129. 35; 149. 7-8; 173. 5, 12, 29, etc.
आयुधागार: Āyudhāgāra — arsenal: meddling with it was punished with death. M. 163. 51; 215. 44; 217. 16; 227. 174.
आयुर्दा: Āyurdā — R. in Śākadvīpa. Bhā. V. 20. 26.
आयुर्दान: Āyurdāna — a Pārāvata god. Br. II. 36. 14.
आयुर्वेद: Āyurveda — originated from Dhanvantari;1 from the east face of Brahmā;2 one of the eighteen vidyas;3 begins in Dvāpara;4 Bharadvāja was the compiler of the Āyurveda and other sciences connected with medicine; it was divided into eight parts each of which was given to one of his disciples.5 1) Bhā. II. 7. 21; VIII. 8. 35; IX. 17. 4; Br. III. 67. 18; Vā. 92. 16; Vi. IV. 8. 10. 2) Bhā. III. 12. 38. 3) Br. II. 35. 88; Vi. III. 6. 28; Vā. 61. 79. 4) M. 144. 22; Vā. 58. 23; Br. II. 31. 23. 5) Vā. 92. 22; Br. III. 67. 24.
आयुर्व्रतम्: Āyurvratam — in honour of Śiva. M. 101. 22.
आयुष: Āyuṣa — the son of Aiḍa. Vā. 1. 192.
आयुष्मत्: Āyuṣmat (I) — the father of Ṛṣabha-Hari by Ambu-dhārā. Bhā. VIII. 13. 20.
Āyuṣmat (II) — a son of Uttānapāda. Br. II. 36. 89.
Āyuṣmat (III) — a son of Praḥlāda. M. 6. 9; Vi. I. 21. 1.
आयुष्मत्य: Āyuṣmatya — an apsarasa gaṇa from Sūrya. Vā. 69. 55.
आयुष्मन्त: Āyuṣmanta — a gaṇa of gods. Br. IV. 1. 122.
आरण्य: Āraṇya — a madhyamādhvaryu; a Prajāpati and father of five deva gaṇas of the Cākṣuṣa epoch.1 Son of Atri.2 1) Br. II. 33. 15; 36. 68. 2) Vā. 62. 58.
आरण्यवाक्य: Āraṇyavākyas — passages of the Āraṇyaka portion of the Vedas. Br. III. 21. 55.
आरब्ध: Ārabdha — the son of Setu and father of Gāndhāra. Bhā. IX. 23. 15; Vi. IV. 17. 3-4.
आरम्भयज्ञ: Ārambhayajñas — for Kṣatriyas. Br. II. 29. 55; Vā. 57. 50.
आराधि: Ārādhi — a son of Jayatsena. Vā. 99. 231.
आराधित: Ārādhita — a son of Jayatsena and father of Ayutāyu. Vi. IV. 20. 4.
आराम: Ārāma — Laying out parks at the auspicious hour — also Udyāna;1 in Tripuram;2 punishment for misuse of.3 1) M. 58. 1 and 52. 2) Ib. 130. 5. 3) Ib. 227. 30; Vā. 101. 160.
आरुणि: Āruṇi (II) — (Ātreya) a sage of the epoch of the third Sāvarṇa Manu. Br. IV. 1. 79.
Āruṇi (IV) — the fifteenth Vyāsa, Vedaśiras, the avatār of the Lord. Vā. 23. 166.
Āruṇi (V) — a sage of the XIth epoch of Manu. Vi. III. 2. 31.
Āruṇi (VI) — the first of the madhyadeśas. Vā. 61. 9.
आर्जव: Ārjava — a pupil of Bāṣkali. Br. II. 35. 6.
आर्तव: Ārtavas (I) — five sons of Brahmā: represented by Agniṣvāttas. Br. II. 21. 152; 23. 75-77; 28. 16 ff.
Ārtavas (II) — five sons of Ṛtus: These are half months: Represent Pitṛs;1 sections of the year; depend on the seasons.2 1) M. 141. 14 and 57; Vā. 30. 18, 22. 2) Vā. 70. 14; Br. II. 13. 19-25, 149.
आर्द्रक: Ārdraka — the father of Dhṛti. Br. III. 71. 124.
आर्द्रा: Ārdrā — the name of a constellation. Vā. 82. 3.
आर्द्रानन्दकरि: Ārdrānandakari — Tṛtīyāvratam: sacred to Bhavānī sit-ting with Mahādeva: to be done for four months, once in every pakṣa: the performer enjoys the world of Rudrāṇī. M. 64 (whole).
आर्य: Ārya (II) — collective name of Aṅgiras' sons1 as oppo-sed to Mleccha.2 Their country was Bhāratavarṣa; side by side with Mleccha in Kaliyuga.3 1) Bhā. IX. 4. 2; Br. II. 16. 24. 2) M. 227. 198; 114. 20. 3) M. 121. 46-51; 273. 25; 274. 37.
आर्यक: Āryaka (I) — the father of Dharmasetu. Bhā. VIII. 13. 26.
Āryaka (II) — a Kādraveya nāga. Br. III. 7. 33.
Āryakas — caste equal to Brāhmaṇa in Plakṣadvīpa. Vi. II. 4. 17.
आर्यका: Āryakā — a R. in Krauñca-dvīpa. Bhā. V. 20. 21.
आर्यसमय: Āryasamaya — does not accept the duties of Pākhaṇḍas. Bhā. V. 14. 29.
आर्यव: Āryava — one of the three disciples of Rathītara. Vā. 61. 3.
आर्या: Āryā — Dvaipāyanī — a R. visited by Balarāma. Bhā. X. 79. 20.
आर्यावर्त: Āryāvarta — twenty-five of Ikṣvāku's sons were rulers over this territory; given to Upadraṣṭa by Paraśurāma. Bhā. IX. 6. 5; 16. 22.
आर्वत: Ārvata — a sage by tapas. Br. II. 32. 99.
आर्ष: Ārṣa (I) — a form of marriage; girls to be given in the Ganges-Yamuna doab. M. 106. 8; Vi. III. 10. 24.

Ārṣa (II) — origin of; when the whole world was in a state of cetana-acetana knowledge like the fish in the water, the truth influenced by cetana arises with guṇa; kāryam is the result of kāraṇa or reason; so also viṣaya is the result of viṣayitva and artha of arthitva; by this Mahat and others function by degrees. Vā. 59. 63-8.
आर्षकम्: Ārṣakam — Ṛṣis, past and future. M. 145. 65.
आर्षभ: Ārṣabhas — a branch of Aṅgirasa. Vā. 65. 107.
आर्षभि: Ārṣabhi — the street with the constellations of Pūrva and Uttara Phalguni and Magha; in madhyama mārga. Br. III. 3. 49; M. 124. 56.
आर्ष्टिषेण: Ārṣṭiṣeṇa (I) — a chief Gandharva who sings Rāma's glory in Kimpuruṣa; came to see Parīkṣit practising prāyopa-veśa. Knew the yoga-power of Hari. Bhā. V. 19. 2; I. 19. 10; II. 7. 45.
Ārṣṭiṣeṇa (II) — the son of Śala. Br. III. 67. 6; Vā. 92. 5.
Ārṣṭiṣeṇa (III) — a rajaṛṣi becoming a Brāhmaṇa. Vā. 91. 116.
Ārṣṭiṣeṇa (IV) — a mantrakṛt — a Pañcārṣeya Bhārgava. Br. II. 32. 105; M. 145. 99; 195. 34.
Ārṣṭiṣeṇas — a Bhārgava branch — Kṣatradvijas. Br. III. 1. 100; 66. 87; 67. 6; Vā. 92. 6.
आर्हतम्: Ārhatam — one of the six darśanas. Vā. 104. 16.
आर्हण: Ārhaṇa (Arhaṇa — Bur.) a chief attendant on Hari. Bhā. II. 9. 14.
आलम्ब: Ālambas — a class of sages. M. 200. 17.
आलम्बा: Ālambā — a daughter of Khaśā, and a Rākṣasī, after whom came the Ālambeya gaṇa. Br. III. 7. 138; Vā. 69. 170.
आलम्बि: Ālambi — a Śrutaṛṣi: the chief author of the Yajurveda of the Eastern recension. Br. II. 33. 6.
आलम्बिरादि: Ālambirādi — of the Prācyas; also trayodaśyādayaḥ. Vā. 61. 9.
आलम्बेयगण: Ālambeyagaṇa — a Rākṣasa clan after Ālambā. Br. III. 7. 140.
आलम्बेय: Ālambeyas — a cruel Rākṣasa gaṇa from Ālambā. Vā. 69. 172.
आलयम्: Ālayam — temple for Iśvara. — (see Āyatanam);1 or a place of residence.2 1) Vā. 30. 279; 91. 29; 101. 214. 2) Ib. 50. 15, 17, 22 and 35.
आलोक: Āloka — the lokas which spring from Aloka.1 Ākāśa that seems to exist to our eyes.2 1) Br. II. 19. 151-3, 187; 21. 155; M. 123. 47; 124. 93. 2) Vā. 49. 145 and 176.
आवटी: Āvaṭī — a pupil of Yājñavalkya. Br. II. 35. 29.
आवन्त्य: Āvantya — a Brāhmaṇa pupil of Sukarman. Imparted in his turn the samhitas to his pupils. Bhā. XII. 6. 77-80.
आवन्त्यौ: Āvantyau — the two sons of Jayasena so called. Bhā. IX. 24. 39.
आवरण: Āvaraṇa — a son of Bharata and Pāñcajanī. Bhā. V. 7. 3.
आवर्तक: Āvartakas — clouds of the Pakṣaja class that rain copiously. Br. II. 22. 40; IV. 28. 63.
आवर्तन: Āvartana — An upadvīpa to Jambūdvīpa. Bhā. V. 19. 30.
आवसथ्य: Āvasathya — a son of Śamsya Agni. Vā. 29. 12.
आवसथ्यम्: Āvasathyam — the lower lip of the personified Veda. Vā. 104. 84.
आवह: Āvaha (I) — a wind that helps Āgneya clouds to rain:1 one of the seven Maruts;2 controls the mūka clouds.3 1) Br. II. 22. 34; III. 5. 82; 71. 112. 2) M. 163. 32. 3) Vā. 51. 32, 49; 67. 114.
Āvaha (II) — a son of Gāndini. Vā. 96. 111.
आवाहनी: Āvāhanī — a mudrā Devī. Br. IV. 42. 2.
आविक्षिः: Āvikṣiḥ — a true son of his father in virtuous qualities. Vā. 86. 8.
आविर्मुखि: Āvirmukhi — one of the eastern entrances of the city of Puramjana: allegorically the right eye. Bhā. IV. 25. 47; 29. 10.
आविहोत्र: Āvihotra — an Ātreya and sage. Br. II. 32. 114.
आविर्होत्र: Āvirhotra — a son of Ṛṣabha; a sage and a bhāgavata; asked as to the truth of karmayoga by Nimi, the sage in-structed the king that karma, akarma and vikarma are Veda-vāda and not laukika which thesis he expanded. Bhā. V. 4. 11; XI. 2. 21; 3. 41-55.
आशय: Āśaya — the cause of karmas which in turn lead to birth. Vā. 8. 30.
आशी: Āśīs — the daughter of Bhaga and Siddhi. Bhā. VI. 18. 2.
आशौचम्: Āśaucam — for father's death 10 days for Brāhmaṇas, 12 days for Kṣatriyas, 15 days for Vaiśyas, and a month for the Śūdras. M. 18. 1-3.
आश्रम: Āśramas (āśramadharma) — four, Brahmacarya, gṛhasta, vānaprastha and bhikṣuka; duties: — Brahmacarya: study by service to guru and begging food; gṛhasta: the source and strength of all āśramas; those celibate do penance, sacrifice, give birth to sons, perform śrāddha, learn the Vedas and give gifts of food; dārāgni, guests, sacrifice and śrāddha; become devapitṛs; vānaprastha: bathe in morning and evening and on ceremonials; eating of fruits and roots, non-theft, purity, sympathy and non-injury — ten kinds of dharma; Bhikṣu: daṇḍi, mekhali, and lying in ground floor.1 A reference to the fifth āśrama;2 will be lost at the end of Kaliyuga when anarchy prevails.3 1) Bhā. VII. 12. 1-31; 13. 1-10; 14. to the end; M. 141. 61-2; 248. 16; Vā. 8. 177-88; 23. 82; 33. 27; 56. 68; 61. 167; Vi. III. 8. 20; ch. 9 (whole). 2) Br. II. 16. 15; III. 15. 37-8. 3) M. 47. 257.
आश्रायणि: Āśrāyaṇis — a group of sages of Kaśyapa gotra. M. 199. 2.
आश्लेषा: Āśleṣā — on the left hind foot of the Śiśumāra.1 Its im-portance for śrāddha;2 the seventh nakṣatra.3 1) Bhā. V. 23. 6; Br. II. 24. 135. 2) Br. III. 18. 5. 3) Vā. 82. 5.
आश्वलायन: Āśvalāyana — a son of Sahiṣṇu avatār of the Lord. Vā. 23. 213.
आश्वलायनि: Āśvalāyani — a pravara of Aṅgiras. M. 196. 13.
आषाढ: Āṣāḍha(daśami) — a manvantara for śrāddha. M. 17. 7-8.
आषाढम्: Āṣāḍham — sacred to Aṅgāraka, and for performing śrāddha. Br. II. 21. 76; 24. 133; III. 18. 10; Vā. 53. 108; 66. 51; 82. 10.
आसनम्: Āsanam — Svastikam, Padmam and Ardhāsanam — the sitting posture of the Pāśupata yoga;1 a kind of dharaṇā.2 1) Vā. 11. 12-14. 2) Vā. 104. 24.
आसङ्ग: Āsaṅga — the son of Śvaphalka and Gāndini. Bhā. IX. 24. 16.
आसव: Āsava — also Pānam; different kinds of; forbidden to Brāhmaṇas, widows and girls. Br. IV. 7. 63.
आसारण: Āsāraṇa — the Yakṣa presiding over the month Nabhasya. Bhā. XII. 11. 38.
आसुर: Āsura — a form of marriage. Vi. III. 10. 24.
आसुरायण: Āsurāyaṇa — a pupil of Pārāśarya Kauthuma.1 His descendants were Kaśyapagotrakaras.2 1) Br. II. 35. 46. 2) M. 199. 3.
आसुरी: Āsurī (I) — the name of the entrance of the west of the city of Puramjana; allegorically the organ of procreation. Bhā. IV. 25. 52; 29. 14.

Āsurī (II) — a pupil of Kapila from whom he learnt Sāṅkhya; a siddha;1 did not comprehend Hari's māyā;2 was invited for the Rājasūya of Yudhiṣṭhira.3 1) Bhā. I. 3. 10; III. 24. 17; VI. 15. 14. 2) Bhā. IX. 4. 57. 3) Bhā. X. 74. 9.
Āsurī (III) — the queen Devatājit and mother of Deva-dyumna. (Asuri-Burnouf). Bhā. V. 15. 3.
Āsurī (IV) — the chief author of the recension of the Yajur Veda of the middle country;1 a Brahmaṛṣi.2 1) Br. II. 35. 12. 2) M. 102. 18.
Āsurī (V) — a son of Brahmā. Vā. 101. 338.
आसुरीवेल: Āsurīvela — part of night when Nanda entered the Yamunā and was carried to Varuṇa by an Asura. Bhā. X. 28. 2.
आहवनीय: Āhavanīya (Havyavāhana) — a sacred fire. Br. III. 72. 25; Vā. 29. 11; 30. 107; 97. 25; 106. 41.
आहार्य: Āhārya — an Aṅgirasa and a mantrakṛt:1 Father of Urukṣava.2 1) Br. II. 32. 109: Vā. 59. 100. 2) M. 49. 38.
आहुक: Āhuka — A son of Punarvasu and father of Devaka and Ugrasena and Dhṛti (Vā.);1 a prince who had thousands of sons.2 Hated by Kaṃsa.3 Consulted by Kṛṣṇa on the eve of attack on Jarāsandha. His defence in the third campaign of Jarāsandha.4 Met Kṛṣṇa at the council hall, and wel-comed him after the Kurukṣetra war.5 Went to Syamanta-pañcaka for solar eclipse.6 An ideal ruler; married Kāśi king's daughter.7 Specialist in chariot war;8 Āhukī was his sister, married to Āhukāndha;9 had 800 lakhs of horses, 21,000 elephants with silver and gold chains in east and west directions; equal to great Bhoja;10 informed of happenings in Prabhāsa.11 1) Bhā. IX. 24. 20-21; Vā. 96. 120-123; Vi. IV. 14. 15-16; Br. III. 71. 120-121. 2) Bhā. I. 14. 28; X. 90. 42. 3) Ib. X. 36. 24 [28]; X[50 (V) 8]. 4) Ib. X [51 (V) 26]. 5) Ib. X. [67 (V) 42]; 80. [13]. 6) Ib. X. 82. 5. 7) Br. III. 71. 128; M. 44. 70. 8) Vā. 96. 121-2; Br. III. 71. 122-3. 9) Vā. 96. 127; M. 44. 66-70. 10) Br. III. 71. 123-127; Vā. 96. 121-126; M. 44. 67-68. 11) Vi. V. 37. 59.
आहुका: Āhukās — the people of an eastern kingdom. Br. II. 16. 52; Vā. 45. 121.
आहुकान्ध: Āhukāndha — married sister of Āhuka; father of two sons and a daughter. Vā. 96. 127; Br. III. 71. 127.
आहुकी: Āhukī — the daughter of Punarvasu and sister of Āhuka (s.v.) the queen of the king of Avanti (Āhukāndha). Bhā. IX. 24. 21; Br. III. 71. 121 and 127; M. 44. 66; Vā. 96. 120, 127; Vi. IV. 14. 15.
आहृति: Āhṛti — a son of Vastu. Vā. 95. 37.
आहृत्य: Āhṛtya — an Apsaras gaṇa from Brahmā. Br. III. 7. 18.
आह्वय: Āhvaya — one of the names in the third marutgaṇa. Vā. 67. 126.
